findings.finding: US frac spreads, the driver of DynaEnergetics volumes, averaged about 191 in Q3 2026. That is about 5% above Q2's 182 (when DynaEnergetics sales rose 13% sequentially) and +14-28 spreads year over year in every week. Early-Q4 weeks ran 194-203 against 178-179 a year ago. Against that, the broader pressure-pumping read was soft: Halliburton's North America revenue fell 5% sequentially on lower US Land pressure pumping, and Liberty's adj. EBITDA fell 6% sequentially. Liberty did guide to a milder-than-normal Q4 seasonal decline. Net: DynaEnergetics volume supports the 'higher completion activity' assumption in the Q3 guide and a less seasonal Q4, but pricing is not helped.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 print came in at the high end of guidance with DynaEnergetics +13% sequentially, and the stock rose +15.5% (baseline). The Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 prints, on weak energy and a soft outlook, fell -18.6% and -33.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has slid 30% from its August peak while Q3 and early-Q4 frac counts held above Q2 and well above last year. If the market were pricing completion activity, BOOM would not have round-tripped the Q2 pop. The direction is muddied by Halliburton's softer US Land read, so this is sized small.

Liberty Q3 2026 (milder Q4 decline, supports): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001694028/000169402826000055/q32026-earningsrelease.htm. Industry proxies, not company numbers.

findings.finding: Street revenue consensus for Q3 ($154.27M Earnings Whispers, $156.4M Investing.com) sits below the low end of the company's own guide ($158-168M). In Q2 DMC printed $157.0M against a ~$146M consensus, at the high end of its guide. A print anywhere inside the guide is therefore a 2-8% revenue beat against the street.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue at the high end of guide, EPS beat against a -$0.12 forecast, stock +15.5%. Q1 2026 (Apr 30) +36.1%. Q4 2025 (Feb 23) -33.0% on a weak quarter and outlook. The name moves hard on whether the quarter clears the bar.
findings.why_not_priced: A consensus below the guide floor says the street does not believe the guide. If it did, estimates would sit at $158-168M. The price, back at its pre-Q2 level, shows the same disbelief. The finding lands inside what the company already guided, so it is held to a modest size.

findings.finding: The Arcadia minority holder's put on the remaining 40% became exercisable on 2026-09-06. The stake was valued at about $162M at the 2021 deal, and the redeemable NCI was carried at $187.1M at June 30. DMC can settle all in cash or 20% cash / 80% convertible, mandatorily redeemable preferred (conversion capped at 19.9% of shares, three annual cash redemptions). DMC had $28.6M of cash and $59.1M of debt at June 30. No 8-K has been filed since July 29, so the Q3 release or 10-Q is the first place an exercise, a standstill or a DMC call would show. On the Q2 call the CEO said 'we have absolutely no idea' whether the partner will exercise. The stock began a steady slide right after the exercise date (6.97 on Sept 4 to 5.36).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has resolved this put. The December 2024 extension of the put to September 2026 and the rejection of Steel Connect's funding proposal (Feb 2025) are the nearest precedents; their reactions are not in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Its status is unknown to everyone outside the company. The slide since Sept 6 on light volume suggests part of an exercise is already in the price. Sign rule: an exercise settled 80% in preferred buys out a segment that earned $5.5M (DMC share) plus $3.7M (NCI share) of Q2 adj. EBITDA, i.e. accretive cash flow, at the cost of up to 19.9% dilution and three years of cash redemptions. No exercise leaves the overhang in place. Net near zero, slightly negative, with wide range.
findings.independence: Put date and terms: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34067/000003406724000165/dmc-arcadiaputcallextensio.htm. NCI balance: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000034067/000003406726000047/boom-exx991_2026q2.htm. EDGAR filing list shows no 8-K after 2026-07-29: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000034067&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40

findings.finding: The US Midwest aluminum premium, Arcadia's main input-cost driver (aluminum was +79% YoY in Q2 and 'keeps us awake at night'), eased from a record $1.19/lb in June to $1.09/lb by Sept 11, 2026. That is modest relief on Arcadia margins in Q3/Q4. It could also trim the price-driven part of Arcadia sales, which management said was the larger part of Q2's +9%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Arcadia's Q2 margin recovery (13.6% vs 6.9% in Q1) came with the +15.5% Q2 reaction. Arcadia supply problems in Q1 came with the weak Q4/Q1 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a public commodity series, so it is likely partly priced. The transmission to Arcadia margins is inference: the company has not confirmed it and passes price through with a lag. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: Q2 call aluminum commentary: https://www.webull.com/news/15364520756012032. A proxy, not a company number.

findings.finding: DynaEnergetics booked a $1.5M tariff refund in Q2, and the Q3 guide explicitly assumes none. Management said it is 'still filing for more refunds'. Any further refund recognised in Q3 is upside to the $10-13M EBITDA guide (1.5M is about 13% of the midpoint), but it is a one-off.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 refund was part of the print that rose +15.5%. Analysts asked about it explicitly and management called it non-recurring.
findings.why_not_priced: It is excluded from guidance by design and its timing is unforecastable. It sits below the quality line, so it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: Q2 release notes $1.5M of refunds in DynaEnergetics' adj. EBITDA: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000034067/000003406726000047/boom-exx991_2026q2.htm (same company, different document).

findings.finding: Into the print, the stock (5.36) has fully reversed its Q2 reaction (pre-print 5.42, peak 7.66) on light volume, with no 8-K, no analyst action and no insider filing found to explain it. The bar implied by price is therefore close to where it stood before a print that beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Coming into Q2 off a similar drawdown, the stock rose +15.5%. Coming into Q4 2025, it fell -33.0%. Drawdowns have not reliably predicted direction.
findings.why_not_priced: This is itself a price observation, so by definition it is priced. A drawdown without a cause in the record is not evidence of over-reaction (the cause may be the Arcadia put or the energy tape). Kept at a token size.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The slight upward lean cuts against the 20-day downtrend and the 1.44 put/call OI, but the option market here is 139 contracts at a 46% spread, so the tape is the stronger statement, and that statement is mostly the unresolved Arcadia put overhang.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown in a microcap is worth 0): positioning/round-trip finding cut from +0.8 to +0.2
Lesson 2 (one-offs sized as one-offs): tariff-refund upside cut from +0.3 to +0.15
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): kept the Arcadia put at -0.5 with a wide two-sided range, after asking what the buyout buys (accretive segment cash flow vs dilution and redemptions)
Lesson 6 (bar sourced; inside the guide): left the consensus-below-guide finding at +1.0, since two estimate sources agree and the company guide is the reference
